status_observed: 201 Created, with the blank value persisted verbatim, e.g. {"id":"cc52dec0-...","is_active":true,"name":"","code":null,"description":null}
what_is_wrong: The required identifying field (`name`, or `plan_name` on insurance-plans) has no non-empty or trim validation. An empty string and a whitespace-only string are both accepted and stored verbatim, creating unnameable master rows that render as blank entries in every dropdown that consumes them. Because there is no trim, the uniqueness guard is also bypassable: a name that differs from an existing one only by a trailing space is accepted as a new distinct row, so the duplicate-name protection (which correctly returns 409 for an exact match) can be defeated trivially and two visually identical rows can coexist.

Response: 201 {"id":"cc52dec0-8a7f-4e28-9e50-cd916b614b78","is_active":true,"name":"","code":null,"description":null}

  units-of-measure 201 stored='\t'    | empty-string -> 201 name=""
  customer-sources 201 stored='   '   | empty-string -> 201 name=""
  leave-types      201 stored='   '   | empty-string -> 201 name=""
  expense-types    201 stored='  '    | empty-string -> 201 name=""

Duplicate-guard bypass via untrimmed trailing space:

All rows created for this test were deleted afterwards (204 each).
suspected_cause: No min_length/strip validator on the generated write schemas in app/api/v1/masters_lookup.py (the `fields` spec builds plain `str` pydantic fields); uniqueness is enforced only by the DB unique index on the untrimmed value.

what_is_wrong: `default_useful_life_years` accepts a negative integer and persists it. A negative useful life is not a meaningful value for an asset category and will produce nonsense depreciation output wherever this default is consumed. There is no ge=0/gt=0 constraint on the field in the schema and no DB check constraint catching it â€” unlike insurance-plans' amount columns and leave-types' quota columns, which do have check constraints and correctly reject negatives.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/masters_simple.py asset-categories registration â€” `default_useful_life_years` declared as a bare optional int with no ge constraint; no corresponding DB check constraint on the asset_categories table.

status_observed: 200 â€” is_referenced=true and is_referenced=false each return all 9 rows, identical to the unfiltered call
what_is_wrong: The `is_referenced` query parameter (documented in the spec as "Masters Â§3.0's Used/Unused filter â€” omit for both") is accepted but never applied. The lookup-router factory declares the parameter unconditionally for every generated router, but only applies it when the router was registered with a `referenced_by` list. The hsn-sac-codes registration passes no `referenced_by`, so tracks_references is False and the filter branch is skipped. Two mutually exclusive filter values returning the same complete row set means the Used/Unused filter silently does nothing.
